title: HierKV: A Coarse-to-Fine Approach with Vision-Aware Banzhaf Values for Multi-Modal KV Cache Compression

problem.claim: Long and visually rich inputs in multimodal large language model applications increase the memory and latency cost of attention through KV caching.

gap.claim: Existing KV cache compression methods typically optimize a single granularity, which can misallocate cache capacity because layer roles, head functionalities, and instance-level visual reliance are heterogeneous.

contributions.claim: HierKV uses a hierarchical MLLM KV-cache compression scheme that progressively allocates budgets across layers, heads, and tokens.
For layers, HierKV assigns budgets using model-level block importance derived from Banzhaf values together with instance-specific visual sensitivity inferred through attention perturbation.
At the head and token levels, HierKV prioritizes cross-modal interaction heads and performs budgeted top-K token retention within each head.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments across multiple MLLMs and multimodal benchmarks show that HierKV achieves a favorable accuracy-latency-memory trade-off under strict cache budgets.
The authors report substantial decoding speedups and GPU memory reductions compared to strong baselines.

narrative_sequence.summary: MLLM deployment in Web mining applications creates memory and latency costs because inputs are long and visually rich.
Single-granularity KV cache compression can misallocate capacity under heterogeneous layer, head, and instance-level visual requirements.
HierKV allocates cache budgets hierarchically from layers to heads to tokens.
It uses Banzhaf-based model-wise importance and instance-wise visual sensitivity for layer budgets, then prioritizes cross-modal heads and retains top-K tokens within each head.
The authors report favorable accuracy-latency-memory trade-offs, decoding speedups, and GPU memory reductions under strict cache budgets.

source_observation.claim: Cache capacity may need to be allocated across multiple structural levels because layer roles, head functionalities, and instance-level visual reliance are heterogeneous.

interpretation.claim: Compression strategies that model heterogeneous resource importance at progressively finer granularities may avoid misallocation.

application.claim: For multimodal attention caching, consider coarse-to-fine allocation across layers, heads, and tokens.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy generalizes beyond the reported MLLMs, benchmarks, or cache-budget conditions.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the evaluated MLLMs, benchmarks, baselines, cache budgets, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe computational overhead, implementation details, or failure cases.
